subject: Allocation conflict: Bridgewater Q4 surge vs. existing Dedicated commitments
messages:
From: Elena Ross <elena@bridgewater.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@bridgewater.ai
Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: Q4 burst scheduling overlap with committed Dedicated slots

Irene / Monica,

Quick heads-up — our finance and infra teams just finalized a campaign that will require a short burst of Dedicated capacity in mid-November (expected peak Nov 15-19). We submitted the SOW last week (attached: Bridgewater_capacity_SOW_v3.pdf) but I was just told by our ops lead that the dates overlap with another committed customer tranche.

This is time-sensitive: the campaign spend is committed and tied to downstream launch dates. Can Redwood confirm whether we can get the requested capacity or if there will be a prioritization decision? If there is a conflict, we need to understand the escalation path and any commercial remedies (credits/fallback routing).

Thanks,
Elena
Elena Ross
Head of Platform Engineering | Bridgewater AI
elena@bridgewater.ai

Elena —

Thanks for the heads-up and for sending the SOW. Monica and I are looping in Rishi and Markus to get a clear view of the fleet schedule and any contention risk. I'll summarize the current standing and propose options by EOD.

Prelim note: we do have a Reserved tranche that overlaps those dates (committed customer is on a reserved monthly cadence). We can explore three paths: 1) adjust Bridgewater's burst to adjacent dates, 2) temporarily shift some reserved capacity to burst mode with offset credits, or 3) route a portion to compatible region capacity (if latency allows).

I'll follow up with the allocation snapshot and a recommended mitigation. If you can share a hard window for the campaign (start/end times in PST) that helps size the exact hours.

Best,
Irene Choi

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Elena Ross <elena@bridgewater.ai>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Q4 burst scheduling overlap with committed Dedicated slots

Irene / team —

I pulled the fleet allocation print for Nov 12–22 and attached a condensed report (allocation_report_q3.xlsx). Summary: there is a ~36 GPU-hour overlap on Nov 15 between Bridgewater's requested burst (80 GPU-hours) and a committed Reserved customer tranche that cannot be trivially preempted without violating their SLA.

Technical notes: the conflicting tranche is pinned to a pinned-node pool (low-latency requirement) and is running a model variant that requires A100-class machines. Bridgewater's workload can tolerate an A6000 equivalent for non-peak flows, but the peak inference tails are latency-sensitive.

Mitigation options (tech):
- Partial slot rebalancing: move 40 GPU-hours of Bridgewater off-peak to Nov 14/16 (minimal model degradation).
- Cross-region burst: route 20 GPU-hours to our US-east burst pool (adds ~25–40ms RTT).
- Quantized lane: run a 8-bit quantized variant in a higher density pool for up to 20 GPU-hours (risk: potential quality drift).

I'll run a simulation of expected token throughput and tail latency for each option and post results in INF-5421.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: allocation_report_q3.xlsx (xlsx, 220KB)

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ross <elena@bridgewater.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2026 08:16:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Q4 burst scheduling overlap with committed Dedicated slots

Elena —

Appreciate the urgency. Commercially, Bridgewater is a high-priority deal (DW-8743); we want to minimize launch risk while protecting existing commitments. Proposed approach:

1) Short-term (this campaign): accept partial rebalancing + cross-region burst. We'll allocate 40 GPU-hours shifted to Nov 14/16 and 20 GPU-hours to our US-east burst pool. Bridgewater receives a one-time credit for the 20 GPU-hours routed cross-region (pricing adj).

2) Medium-term (next 30 days): reserve an additional 200 GPU-hours as an addendum to the Dedicated contract (subject to approval). This prevents future mid-month contention.

3) Escalation & SLA: if routing degrades latency beyond 50ms of the committed SLO during peak, we'll offer a pro-rated service credit and prioritize on-call escalation to infra.

Action items:
- Elena: confirm whether a 25–40ms cross-region latency is acceptable for the 20 GPU-hour portion.
- Rishi: finalize perf sims and confirm the quantized lane risk if we need to extend capacity further.
- Irene: will draft the addendum term sheet for legal.

We'll treat this as time-sensitive; recommending a 30-min sync today at 2:30pm PST.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Lead, Customer Success – Dedicated
Redwood Inference

---

From: Elena Ross <elena@bridgewater.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: ops@bridgewater.ai
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Q4 burst scheduling overlap with committed Dedicated slots

Monica / Irene —

Thanks for the proposed approach. Two quick points:
1) Cross-region latency of 25–40ms is tolerable for non-critical inference but not for the live personalization tier — we need the critical 40 GPU-hours to remain within 15ms.
2) We need the term addendum drafted and signed within 7 business days to proceed with marketing commitments.

If the reserved tranche cannot be preempted, we request an escalation to provide either (a) an SLA credit commensurate with Bridgewater's launch risk or (b) temporary burst carve-out from any available preemptible pool that preserves the 15ms critical path.

Please advise; we can join the 2:30pm sync.

Best,
Elena

---

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Ross <elena@bridgewater.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2026 17:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: Q4 burst scheduling overlap with committed Dedicated slots

Elena —

Understood. For the critical 40 GPU-hours requiring <=15ms, Rishi confirms we cannot maintain that on cross-region routing. Two immediate next steps we can commit to right now:

1) We will carve a 40 GPU-hour temporary burst from our preemptible reserve pool onto local A100-class nodes for Nov 15 (11:00–19:00 PST) to preserve the 15ms path. This will be treated as a one-off concession — Redwood will absorb operational cost; Bridgewater will receive a 30% usage credit for that slice if az-affinity constraints increase cost.

2) Monica and I will fast-track the 200 GPU-hour addendum and circulate a draft term sheet by EOD tomorrow for signature within 7 business days. Legal will be on a 48-hour review window.

If that meets you halfway, we'll mark the tranche as assigned in INF-5421 and confirm via DocuSign link in the morning.

Irene Choi
Senior Account Lead, Dedicated Deployments
Redwood Inference
irene@redwoodinference.com
